verdict.tagline: A masterpiece of eerie atmosphere dragged down by technical crashes.
for_you_if: you want to explore the sunken city of Rapture
you can look past technical instability
not_for_you_if: you need stable performance without random crashes
you require reliable controller support out of the box
you expect bug-free progression and objectives

claims.claim: Reviewers experience audio cutouts during loud combat moments.

citations.review_text:
Truly Bioshock is one of the best shooters out there,. The story and world are immaculate, I personally really enjoyed the ending I got, and I feel like it's a great throughline for all the themes in the game. I think this game really holds up and is still really fun, and really mezmerizing to play.

A few notes, I played the original PC version, and while I really enjoyed the visuals there were some definite audio problems, mostly once the game gets loud during fights lots of sounds cut out for no reason. You also have to make sure to uncheck "horizontal fov lock" in the settings so the game won't have the harshest POV you've ever seen, I started getting sick. I honestly think it's worth trying the remaster if you have the option and seeing how well it plays. I just am a sucker for that nostalgic older engine and how it feels.

Must play, get it.
unplayable the audio is so bad i cant even get off the main menu

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game crashes upon reaching save points or entering Rapture.

citations.review_text:
Came here to experience a legendary classic. However, I spent two hours troubleshooting crashes.
Watched the plane crash intro 8 times. Tried every “fix” people on the forum and ChatGPT suggested: windowed mode, admin mode, launcher skip, overlays off, input language changes, config edits… and the game still crashes at the very first save point before I can even properly enter Rapture.
This is not just a few technical issues. The game is fundamentally broken on modern systems.
I genuinely wanted to enjoy and love this game, but instead I wasted 2 hours fighting 2007 PC compatibility problems. Lesson learned: always read the reviews before buying old PC classics.
Constant crashes when arriving in Rapture :{

claims.claim: Reviewers feel the remaster alters the original's horror atmosphere by making Rapture more vivid and censoring certain adult content.

citations.review_text:
I really love the OG over the Remake. 

-The remake made rapture alot more vivid in coloring (reducing the horror feeling), 
-added things that werent there before like sealife, signs, and lighting. 
-They censored some of the more adult stuff like the "romance" and "murder" between Ryan and Jolene. 
-And did a total overhaul on things like the menu. 

I feel like the vibe and art style are no where near the same as the OG. Problem is the OG is hard to run on modern pcs... so, this is kinda all we get.

Get the OG if you wanna play the better version imo (more horror and dark) but if you cant, still totally get this one (more laid back and happy)

BioShock Remastered remains one of the greatest immersive shooters ever made. Even years later, Rapture is an unforgettable setting filled with atmosphere, incredible art direction, and some of the best environmental storytelling in gaming. The world feels alive, the soundtrack is phenomenal, and the narrative still holds up remarkably well. Every corner of the city tells its own story, and the blend of exploration, combat, and plasmid abilities keeps the gameplay engaging from beginning to end.

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this version for Apple Silicon Macs.

I played on an M1 Pro, and the performance is simply unacceptable. The frame rate regularly drops into the 35 FPS range, even though this hardware is more than capable of handling a game from 2007. The issue is clearly the port itself, not the machine.

It’s a real shame because the game itself is an absolute masterpiece. If you’re on Windows or console, I highly recommend playing BioShock Remastered. But if you’re using an Apple Silicon Mac.

Amazing game. Terrible Apple Silicon port.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Reviewers encounter repetitive hacking minigames, progress-blocking bugs with missing objectives, and crashes when opening menus or pausing.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the hacking minigame becomes repetitive after being performed many times throughout the playthrough.

citations.review_text:
A classic. If you have not played before and have not had it spoiled, it's a must play. The story is one of the best video games have to offer, as well as the worldbuilding. It's a shame they didn't remake this game from the ground up.

The game does show it's age a bit, but the atmosphere and  world building is one of the best though. I really hope they do it justice with the eventual movie they're going to be releasing.

A few minor complaints - voice acting is very soft by default so it's hard to hear over the screaming of the enemies and the alarm of the cameras/turrets/bots. Speaking of alarms, the sound is obnoxious. Also get ready for a lot of hacking. Mini game is fine, but when you do it a hundred times it's a little tiring.

Big daddies are fun to fight, worldbuilding is great and the plasmid mechanic is really cool. Hack mechanic is a bit too basic and repetitive but other than that, 1000% worth getting the bioshock collection on sale.

I bought BioShock because it's always ranked as one of the best games ever made, and after playing it I can see why. For a game that came out in 2007, it was way ahead of its time. The atmosphere is awesome, the ending was good, and the hacking minigames were a nice break from all the exploring.

That being said, the game definitely shows its age. I ran into quite a few bugs and got stuck on objects multiple times. A couple of times I thought I was going to have to restart my game. Some of the missions where you have to collect items or take pictures also felt pretty slow, and the combat started to get repetitive near the end.

I got the game on sale for about $3, and at that price it's 100% worth buying. It's also not very long—I finished it in around 8 hours—so it's a great game if you're looking for something you can beat in a week.

Gameplay: 7/10
Bugs: 2/10
Price: 10/10
Overall: 8/10

claims.claim: Reviewers experience progress-blocking bugs involving missing or non-spawning objectives such as spider splicers and little sisters.

citations.review_text:
Neptune's bounty is bugged into oblivion. splicers you need to take pictures dont show up. big daddy is down but the little sister is nowhere to be seen. you can miss the grenade launcher pickup easly. i reloaded that level like 3 times. each time something else. first i couldent get the spider splicer to spawn so i got only 2 out 3 photos. next i missed the grenade launcher. third. i took down a rosie big daddy but the little sister wasent even with him and i have no idea what to do. i will replay this mission again after being noted that its broken and making sure i do things right. but the game is just bugged.

EDIT: so i figured some stuff up, not played for a long time. now the pickup was there for the grenade launcher i missed it, the big daddy if not with a little sister you have to wait for him to knock on the circle hole then the little sister comes out. and the spider splicer. maybe it was bug i dont know. but reloading the save doing it again fixed it. so we are left out with the rest of the game which is a masterpiece of story telling. gameplay wise. i know you can disable vita chambers but seeing how slow is to load and save in this game i prefer going back to a vita chamber instead. but i have to ask. whats exactly is remasterd about this version? maybe its hard for me notice but aside from high framerate and 4k resolution i dont see any noticiable graphical change. but because i got the original version as well buying the collection. and i do reccomend buying the collection on a sale. it was cheap and it was worth it for a great game.

ran into a gamebreaking bug that softlocked me. This apparently has existed since the Xbox 360 version and still has not been fixed to this day. It is extremely well documented (links below) and there isn't even a way to console command yourself out of a situation. Completely unacceptable to leave a bug like this in a paid rerelease of such an old game. Shame because the game seemed fun but I don't feel like redoing all of my progress in hopes the bug doesn't trigger a second time.

https://www.reddit.com/r/Bioshock/comments/m0gkbq/gamebreaking_bug_bioshock_remastered_spider/
https://steamcommunity.com/app/409710/discussions/0/350542145691669269/

Gamebreaking bug softlocked my game. Currently stuck at 2/3 photographed spider splicers. Reloaded to fix the bug, annoying but the game is so good it was worth it. Annoying that these bugs will never be fixed but aside from that, the game is amazing.
Game-breaking bug with the splicers -- one of them won't spawn.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Long-term players report progression blockers in specific encounters, high-difficulty ammunition balancing issues, and crashes on multi-core processors.

claims.claim: The game features a specific bug during Sander Cohen's task where failing to defeat the masked Splicers quickly enough prevents the final enemy from spawning, forcing players to reload an earlier save.

citations.review_text: I already played through this game a few years back without problem. Just started playing again the other day and got to the level where you have to take a picture of 3 splicers. Got the first 2 and just went through the level figuring I'd run into the last one eventually. Spent a good hour or so 100% everything in the level leaving no corner untouched. Looked it up and it turns out I ran into a hard lock where the last spawn doesn't trigger in room 5 and the only way to fix is to restart the level. At least this remaster is better than the mess of the oblivion one but never playing this again regardless. Just save the headache and play the original.

Lackluster ending in this game. I took way too long to finish it. 

The weapon mechanics in this game are kind of annoying, Splicers piss me off and defeating Atlas was underwhelming.

ALSO there's a bug in this game that was brough over from the OG version of Bioshock. Task 3 of 4 with Sander Cohen's masterpiece task can put you in a stuck situation when killing all the Splicers with masks, if you don't do this fast enough, the last one will not spawn and you'll be forced to restart the checkpoint from an older save slot.

Going to finish Bioshock 2 at some point to get a better understanding of the lore.

This game was good, but not that great. IMO.

claims.claim: The game suffers from random crashes and compatibility issues when run on hardware with more than four CPU cores, requiring manual fixes or stability patches.

citations.review_text:
8.5/10

Few things are dated in the game.
Art style is very good.

Had no crashes game also has NG+ and a trials mode for additonal content.

Main story is likely 15-20 hours long on the first playtrough.

You can have multiple play styles depending on what tonics you want to have so there is a replay value.

Plenty of plasmids(spells) good vareity,word building.
Tons of word building and lore.

Very low system requirements also played it on my older PCs with no issues.

Cons:For some ppl the remasters crashes a lot more.
Somewhat dated GFX,some visual effects are worse in the remaster than in the OG.
Some weapons or ammo types are just very underpowered on survival difficulty like standard Machinegun and pistol rounds past the very early game.


Good idea to cap fps to a sensiable amount and capping CPU affinity to only 4 core used likely will help to reduce crashes.

Neutral:The game is a much more streamlined game and is also easier than System shock 2.

Default difficulty can become very easy once the player has been built up.
Hard is a good balance.

Survival(very hard) difficulty is actually difficult with very bullet sponge enemies.

Enviorment interactions is good like in genre eg.Shocking water to kill enemies,using fire to melt fire.
Taking an item into fire and using telekinesis to melt the ice.
Placing 6 proxymines into an explosive barrel and then kinesis tossing into a Big-daddy for very big dmg.

[h1] --FIRST OF ALL-- [/h1]
Install those 2 mods from Nexus Mods that I'm going to mention here:
[list]
    [*]"Visual Fixes for Bioshock Remastered"
    [*]"Bioshock Remastered Stability Patches And Bugs Fixes"
[/list]
If you want to enjoy this Remaster, those mods/fixes are REALLY important... The game WILL crash at random, or if you have a CPU with more than 4 cores... and the "Visual Fixes" will restore / fix many things related to the graphics that this Remaster broke for no reason.

[h3]So... let's talk about the game now:[/h3]

I consider this game to be somewhat easy, even on the hardest difficulties like Survivor. If you explore every corner of the game, you’ll end up with 9 First Aid Kits / 9 EVE Hypo Syringes. The story is really good, but halfway through the game, it kind of hits a wall and only starts moving forward again after the halfway point, or around 75% into the game/story.

You can be REALLY creative in this game. The weapons... the Plasmids... the Tonics! There are so many possibilities. You basically decide how you want to play the game (if you want, you can even go on a killing spree using nothing but a wrench after unlocking / using the right Tonics).

In short, if you're interested in this pretty game... follow my tips:
[list]
    [*]Play on "Normal" if this is your first shooter.
    [*]If you have experience with shooters, play on Hard / Survivor.
    [*]Explore every nook and cranny of Rapture, there's always something for you to collect.
    [*]Don't forget about the mods/fixes I mentioned.
    [*]The Shotgun in this game has less range than that damn Shotgun from Doom 3.
[/list]

This was a fantastic game back when it was released, and remains a fabulous game after all these years. Played it first on the Xbox360 of a friend. I am now reliving the whole story and, wow, I absolutely recommended this game to everyone. You can get playthrough after playthrough of enjoyment.

The Remastered version is the only one that does not show any bugs on my Windows 11 laptop; the Original, however, does. BUT, for the Remastered to work properly and truly resemble a remaster, several fixes/mods need to be installed from NexusMods:

1. Bioshock Remastered Stability Patches & Bugs Fixes [this is crucial to avoid crashes]
2. BS1RM - HQ Sound For Video [this comes second in importance; otherwise, the sound will be hugely compressed, thus awful]
3. Localization Fixes
4. HD Texture pack
5. BS1R Visual Fixes "Beta" Atmosphere (2.3.1) [you can also use the normal version]
6. Reflective Water Surface (Remastered version)

One other thing that bothers me with the Remastered: no matter what, the game often and randomly launches in windowed mode and not in fullscreen mode. It's very easy to change that, but it is quite annoying, if only a mere inconvenience.
